messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: Elevated 5xx rate observed at control-plane gateway — metric gateway.response_5xx_rate > 5% over 5m. Auto-pager to #incidents (sev: P1).

maria.sre: saw the alert, looking at Grafana now. region-us-west spike, a lot of 502/504 churn hitting /v1/auth and /v1/org/lookup endpoints.

jake.oncall: I'm on call. attaching current error counts: `auth 5xx ~ 12k/min`, `orglookup 5xx ~ 9k/min`.

lee.eng: possible correlation with recent config-service rollout? I see increased latency around 10:12 UTC on the config-service cluster.

tess.product: customers reporting API failures and webhook retries. @support-ops are there any tickets?

support-ops: we have ~18 customer tickets opened in the last 20m, high-usage customers experiencing failed requests and increased timeouts. No data loss reported yet.

maria.sre: quick triage: control-plane gateway returns 502 when upstreams auth/org/billing return 5xx or timeout. Root causes likely in those dependencies. Starting health-checks.

maria.sre: running quick checks:```
# curl health endpoints
curl -sS https://auth.prod.internal/health || echo FAIL
curl -sS https://org.prod.internal/health || echo FAIL
curl -sS https://billing.prod.internal/health || echo FAIL
```

deploy-bot: config-service rollout v2.14 started at 10:11:24 UTC by lee.eng (deployment/config-service).

jake.oncall: ok that aligns. pause rollout? lee, can you abort or rollback config-service?

lee.eng: rolling back to v2.13 now (`kubectl rollout undo deployment/config-service -n controlplane`). Doing a scaled restart on auth & org as well to clear any stuck connections.

maria.sre: while rollback in progress, enable circuit-breaker on gateway for org lookup and auth to reduce cascading failures. Adding a temporary 3s timeout and 2 retries to org auth upstreams.

maria.sre: (note) enabling stale-cache mode for org lookup so control plane can serve cached metadata for 15m TTL. This reduces dependency pressure but may serve slightly out-of-date org names.

lee.eng: rollback finished. auth pods restarted, org pods restarting. Observability shows error tail off but still noisy.

maria.sre: logs snippet from gateway:```
2026-03-15T10:18:12Z gateway ERROR upstream auth timed out after 5s status=504 request_id=abc123
2026-03-15T10:18:13Z gateway ERROR upstream org lookup returned 502 status=502 request_id=def456
```

jake.oncall: customer impact assessment: approx 11% of hosted API requests returning 5xx over last 10m; Dedicated customers on reserved capacity showing <1% errors. Most transactional failures are during token validation and org metadata fetch.

tess.product: prioritize high-uptime customers: can we route them to dedicated control-plane instances (if pinned) or bypass expensive org lookups?

maria.sre: plan: 1) keep rollback and restarts 2) enable cache/stale-mode for org lookup 3) apply temporary rate-limits on non-critical management endpoints to free capacity 4) monitor for 30m, then lift mitigations.

support-ops: informing top-25 customers via status page and support DMs. ETA for broader status update?

jake.oncall: publish initial status update in 10m after confirming error rate trending down. @sre-lead can you join for escalation and postmortem ownership?

sre-lead: joining. if errors don't drop to <2% in 20m, escalate to full incident with postmortem timeline.

maria.sre: telemetry update: after rollback + restarts + cache mode the 5xx rate dropped from 11% -> 2.7% over 8 minutes. Still seeing intermittent spikes tied to billing service timeouts for some long-running checks.

lee.eng: investigating billing service connection pool exhaustion — increasing replica count and adjusting DB connection limits. Patch rolling now.

deploy-bot: deployment/billing-service scaled from 3 -> 6 replicas at 10:27 UTC (triggered by lee.eng).

maria.sre: gateway rules adjusted: backend timeout for billing endpoints shortened to 4s, circuit opened at 80% error rate. This prevents billing slowdowns cascading to auth/org.

jake.oncall: inbound request rate normalized. Rolling window shows 5xx ~ 1.2% last 5m. Preparing status update: "Partial outage affecting control-plane API (org/auth). Mitigations in place; rollback and scaling performed; customers may see intermittent 5xx. No data loss. Engineers continue to monitor."

tess.product: ok please include customer-facing guidance: avoid mass token refreshes and retried jobs for 30m.

support-ops: posted status update and sent proactive emails to the impacted account list.

maria.sre: recommend keeping stale-cache mode for additional 20m and then gradually restore normal mode if 5xx < 0.5% for 15m.

sre-lead: agreed. Jake, hold the channel open for handoff at end of shift. If it stabilizes we'll mark P1 mitigated -> monitoring.

jake.oncall: handing off to night-oncall @maria.sre at 11:00 UTC. I'll update the pager rotation to follow up. Good work everyone, please add notes to the incident timeline for postmortem. :thumbsup:

maria.sre: acknowledged, I'll continue monitoring and collect logs and runbook steps. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-00432 and assigning to SRE.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-00432 created and linked to thread (severity: P1 -> mitigated->monitoring).

maria.sre: final note: primary root cause appears to be config-service rollout triggering resource pressure and connection churn in auth/org, amplified by billing timeouts. Action items for postmortem: improve rollout canaries for control-plane services, add connection-pool autosizing, and default stale-cache fallback.

support-ops: closing customer DMs as we've sent follow-ups and they're accepting the current mitigation plan.

jake.oncall: marking handoff complete. last observed 5xx rate 0.9% at 10:50 UTC. leaving channel to oncall rotation.

maria.sre: switching channel state to monitoring. will update incident timeline with timestamps and CLIs used.

sre-lead: thanks team. postmortem TOC in the ticket.
